text:
Owen Tippett's season has been a strange mix. He's scored in his last two games, against Buffalo and then on the power play in Ottawa, and he has 4 goals in 19 games, almost exactly what his chances deserve. But his ice time is down three minutes from his usual over the last ten, to about 13 and a half a night, and his chance quality has dropped to 0.83 expected goals per 60 from 1.22 last season, when he scored 28.

Five on five is where the minutes have gone. The Flyers take only 39% of the expected goals with him on the ice, more than five points worse than without him. For a player with his tools, top-end speed in the 98th percentile and a shot in the 96th, that's a usage puzzle more than a talent one.

Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking explains the style: 60% of his shots came off the rush last season, and he carried the puck in on 54% of his entries. When the Flyers play fast, he's dangerous. We'd watch whether the recent goals win his minutes back.
headline: Owen Tippett is scoring on fewer minutes
